questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A drought and the year it is dated to
questions.learningObjective: Assess uncertainty in a drought date

stimulus.body: A drought dated to 1177 BCE from one tree's rings could shift by several years if that tree's rings were miscounted by one.

questions.stem: How much could a single miscounted ring shift the date?

options.text: Not at all, because rings are infallible
By at least one year, and possibly more
By exactly a century
By zero, since droughts have no dates

questions.explanation: One miscounted ring shifts the date by at least a year, and errors can compound, so single-site dates carry real uncertainty.
questions.hint: What is the minimum effect of one error?
